title: The sea
hook: trapped at the sea, the people panic, and Musa says: my Lord is with me, He will guide me

segments.voice: Yesterday: the magicians, the experts who knew a trick when they saw one. Your line was they knew the real thing. Did you admit one thing you got wrong? Day fifty-three.

There's a kind of tight spot everyone knows. The bill you can't pay and the one after it. The diagnosis. The phone call at night. Behind you, the thing you ran from. In front, a wall. Musa has led the Children of Israel out of Egypt by night. At sunrise, Pharaoh's army comes after them. And they reach the edge of the sea. Water in front. Chariots behind. The Qur'an says that when the two groups could see each other, Musa's people said: we are caught. It's over. And Musa answers them with one sentence. Today: the sea.
screen: `BEHIND: THE ARMY.` → `IN FRONT: THE WATER.` → `WE ARE CAUGHT.`

segments.voice: Surah ash-Shu'ara. Musa says: kalla. No. Never. Then, in Pickthall's old translation, "my Lord is with me," and he will guide me. Look at what he doesn't say. He doesn't say, I have a plan. He doesn't say, the sea will part. He doesn't know yet what will happen. He knows only who is with him, and that the way will be shown. Then, and only then, the instruction: strike the sea with your staff. There's that staff again, the one he leaned on and knocked leaves down with. He strikes, and the sea splits, each side standing like a great mountain. The people cross. Pharaoh's army follows them in, and the sea closes. Surah Yunus adds a detail that stops readers every time. As Pharaoh is drowning, he says: I believe that there is no god but the One the Children of Israel believe in. And he's told: now? When you rebelled before? The Qur'an says his body will be kept as a sign for those after him. And this day didn't end at the shore. A hadith in Bukhari says that when the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came to Medina, he found the Jews there fasting on the tenth of Muharram, the day of Ashura. He asked why, and they said: it's the day Allah saved Musa. So he fasted it too, and told Muslims to. To this day, many Muslims fast on Ashura, and remember Musa at the sea. For Shia Muslims, Ashura is also the day of mourning for Husayn, the Prophet's grandson, killed at Karbala. One day, holding more than one memory.
screen: `KALLA — NO. NEVER.` · `MY LORD IS WITH ME.` · `STRIKE THE SEA WITH YOUR STAFF.` · `ASHURA — THE DAY MUSA WAS SAVED.` · then, large: `HE WILL GUIDE ME.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: in a tight spot, say: He is with me. Settle, and breathe. Find the tight spot in your life right now, the place where it feels like water ahead and trouble behind. You don't have to solve it. Just stand at the edge of it for a moment. Then, on a slow breath out, if you pray, say: my Lord is with me; He will guide me. If you don't pray, you might say: I'm not alone in this. Say it several times, slowly, and let the next step be the only one you need to see. The bell holds the time.
The sea. Water in front, an army behind, and a man who said: my Lord is with me; He will guide me. Today's word.
Your line: my lord is with me. When today corners you, say it once before you look for the way out. Day fifty-three.

howItsDone: Many Muslims fast on the day of Ashura, the tenth of Muharram, in remembrance of Musa's rescue at the sea; for Shia Muslims, Ashura is also the day of mourning for Imam Husayn at Karbala.

fork.setup: you're with Musa at the edge of the sea. Pharaoh's army is in sight behind you. everyone is shouting: we are caught. what does Musa say?
options: no. my Lord is with me; He will guide me.
fork.reveal: kalla, no: my Lord is with me; He will guide me. only then comes the command to strike the sea with his staff.

original.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 26:62: "no; my Lord is with me; He will guide me."

trapdoor: what you thought: a miracle where the sea split.
what it means: before the sea split, Musa said my Lord is with me; He will guide me, not knowing yet what the way would be.
what a scholar hears: kalla is a strong refusal, no, never; in the Arabic, ma'iya, with me, comes before rabbi, my Lord; a hadith in Bukhari links the rescue to the fast of Ashura.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2004 (the fast of Ashura and Musa's rescue)

notes: Only the fragment 'my Lord is with me' is quoted as Pickthall 26:62; please verify it appears exactly so. The rest of the verse is paraphrased.

Hadith number (Bukhari 2004) cited from memory. The hadith includes the Prophet saying Muslims have more right to Musa; the script omits that line to avoid anything that could read as a comparison. Confirm.
Shia observance of Ashura (mourning for Husayn at Karbala) mentioned without ranking. Confirm wording.
10:90–92 (Pharaoh's belief at drowning, his body kept as a sign) paraphrased; interpretations of 'body kept' vary.
'Each side standing like a great mountain' paraphrases 26:63 (kal-tawdi al-'azim).
